title: Prefix cabinet: First qualifying slip
summary: For each lowercase word, consider each of its nonempty prefixes and count how many input words begin with that prefix, including repeated words and the word itself. Produce the sum of these counts for each word in input order. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
A character-by-character filing cabinet shares its early drawers among labels with matching prefixes. Mina needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

For each lowercase word, consider each of its nonempty prefixes and count how many input words begin with that prefix, including repeated words and the word itself. Produce the sum of these counts for each word in input order.

Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.

Implement prefixCabinetFirstQualifyingSlip(words, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Trie prefix counts. For each lowercase word, consider each of its nonempty prefixes and count how many input words begin with that prefix, including repeated words and the word itself. Produce the sum of these counts for each word in input order. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
There are at most 64 lowercase English words, each with 1 to 12 letters.

Target time O(total characters); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with trie prefix counts. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each lowercase word, consider each of its nonempty prefixes and count how many input words begin with that prefix, including repeated words and the word itself. Produce the sum of these counts for each word in input order. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [7,10,7,5]. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. This gives 7.
The derived sequence is [5,5,4]. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. This gives 5.
